newsitem.title: USA: OfficeMax accelerates store opening plan.
newsitem.headline: OfficeMax accelerates store opening plan.

text.p: Office supply retailer OfficeMax Inc. said Tuesday it will accelerate its expansion plans for the balance of fiscal 1996 by opening 95 to 100 superstores and increase next year's openings to 125 to 150 stores.
The office products superstore chain, which currently operates over 520 superstores and delivery centres, had previously announced plans for 80 new superstores this year and 80 next year.

"We see a unique and very significant window of opportunity created by the consolidation from three major chains down to two currently taking place in the office products superstore industry," said Michael Feuer, chief executive officer of OfficeMax.
Two weeks ago, rivals Staples Inc., based in Framingham, Mass., and Office Depot, based in Delray Beach, Fla., announced plans to merge.
"During the next 24 months, OfficeMax plans to use a preemptive store opening strategy to gain major market share throughout the United States," Feuer said.
By the end of fiscal 1997, which closes at the end of Jan., 1998, OfficeMax expects to be operating approximately 700 stores in the United States.

Feuer said that OfficeMax, which completed its spin-off from discount store operator Kmart Corp. in July 1995, plans to enter new markets that can support only one store, the majority of which have no competition.
The company also plans to add additional stores in its existing markets, as well as clusters of stores in up to five new major markets.
OfficeMax stock was up 25 cents to $15.75 in morning trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
